title: NYC Bans AI for Elementary and Middle Schools
paragraphs: New York City's public schools will temporarily ban elementary and middle school students from using generative artificial intelligence tools during the upcoming school year, Mayor Zohran Mamdani announced on September 2.
New York City public school students will return to classrooms on September 10.

The one-year ban will apply to "all software that uses student-facing generative AI," the mayor's office said. During this time, city education officials will review all technology tools used in the school system and remove those judged to be unnecessary.

The city also plans to establish twice-yearly AI literacy classes for all public high school students. It will also launch pilot programs allowing some high school students to use some AI platforms under an educator's supervision. Companion chatbots will be prohibited across all grades, officials said.

The ban comes as schools across the country try to manage the use of AI tools in the classroom and elsewhere. Schools are working to teach children how to make use of the technology while preventing them from relying too heavily on it or using it to cheat.
At least 37 states have official AI guidance, but there is no single definition of AI literacy or consensus on how it should be taught.
The Los Angeles school district, where students returned to classrooms in mid-August, is also temporarily blocking access to AI tools on student devices across all grades.
The Los Angeles Unified School District said the ban will remain in place across the country's second-largest school district as officials develop a student AI policy during the school year.
Teachers will still be allowed to use AI for instructional planning and operational tasks.

"Each day when our children come to school, we teach them to ask questions, to challenge assumptions, to interrogate the premise, to ask why. When it comes to AI in our schools, we hold an obligation to do the same," Mayor Mamdani said at a news conference.
